claims.text: The deviation is fixed by the platform's own recorded distances, not by the sparse trace: actual 11.40 km minus recommended 9.90 km is 1.50 km, which exceeds the 1.0 km tolerance, so this trip cannot fall into the no-refund tolerance rows (c) or (e) of POL-RD-24 on any view of the evidence.

POL-RD-21 obliges the driver to inform the rider of the deviation by in-app chat, or verbally with a trip call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation, and the chat log holds only two messages - 'At City Square Mall taxi stand, silver Lexus' at 18:04:07 and the rider's 'ok' at 18:04:37 - both sent before the trip started at 18:05:37, while the trip record's own messages_during_trip list is empty and the deviation was detected at 18:14:48; nothing was sent at or before the point of deviation, so the informing requirement is not met and the deviation is not an agreed one.

The verbal limb of POL-RD-21 is closed as well: the trip record's in_app_calls is empty, and POL-RD-21 says in terms that a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established. The driver's own account - 'Passenger was on a phone call the whole ride so I did not interrupt' - is an admission that he gave no notice at all, and a one-line in-app message was plainly available to him, the rider having read the driver's earlier message at 18:04:44.

The traffic advisory does not establish justification on this record. Its own fields return intersects_route as null, justifies_reroute as null, and the reason 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route', while POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where the traffic data intersects the recommended route at the trip time; the driver's claimed CTE/AYE congestion is therefore unproven, which puts the case in row (d) of POL-RD-24 - not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km - and row (d) refunds the excess distance fare in full.

The driver's assertion that the route 'saved him time' is contradicted by the record: the trip ran 23 min 00 s against a recommended duration of 20.0 min, and the trace runs from 18:05:37 to 18:28:37, so the deviation cost time rather than saving it. Under POL-RD-23 a driver's bare assertion, with no data intersecting the recommended route, does not justify the reroute.

The excess distance fare under POL-RD-24 is the deviation distance times the per-km rate with no surge: 1.50 km x 1.05 SGD/km = 1.58 SGD, and that is exactly the figure the fare ledger carries as refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver.

Both rows of POL-RD-24 open on this trip - row (b), traffic-justified but the rider not informed, and row (d), not traffic-justified - refund the excess distance fare, and the only no-refund row for a deviation over 1 km, row (a), requires the rider to have been informed and to have agreed, which the empty in-trip chat refutes. Whichever way the traffic question is answered, the money is the rider's and the driver's claim fails.

The driver filed this dispute, so the outcome is read against him: under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION means the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands, which leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge - the 1.58 SGD already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver, with both monetary fields null.

No human review follows from value or from the parties: the amount contested is 1.58 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold at which the AI ruling is final at any confidence, and both profiles carry fraud_flags of 0, so no 0.95 confidence is required and POL-GEN-22 requires no escalation.

None of the facts the refund matrix needs is missing or impaired: the trip record, the GPS trace, the chat log, the fare breakdown and the traffic advisory are all COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so POL-GEN-26's escalation for a fact the record cannot establish is not engaged and the deviation, the notification and the fare are all ruleable on this record.

claims.text: POL-RD-21 permits a driver to reroute from the recommended route in response to real-time traffic or congestion, and that is exactly what this record shows. EV-ADVIS-06014-01 is an LTA advisory of type HEAVY_TRAFFIC for Central Expressway (CTE) towards AYE after the Outram Road exit, valid 17:43:57 to 18:55:37, which covers the trip window recorded in EV-TRIP-06014 (started 18:05:37, ended 18:28:37). The driver left the recommended route at the CTE / Outram Road exit at 18:14:48 and rejoined it at Alexandra Road / Henderson Road at 18:26:20 (EV-TRIP-06014), and EV-GPS-06014's trace shows the map-matched road changing from Central Expressway (CTE) to Outram Road between 18:14:07 and 18:14:37. The reroute was a direct response to reported congestion on the corridor the driver was travelling, not a detour for the driver's own purposes.

Whether this reroute is traffic-justified within POL-RD-23 is left open by the evidence itself, and POL-RD-23 is the test that matters: the advisory must intersect the recommended route and overlap the trip window. EV-ADVIS-06014-01 returns intersects_route and justifies_reroute as null and states on its face that the record does not say whether the advisory lies on the recommended route (its 'undetermined' value is 'on the recommended route'). The window limb is satisfied; the intersection limb is not established by the artifact that carries it.

Because the fact 'whether traffic justified the reroute' cannot be established on this record, POL-GEN-26 requires the case to be escalated rather than decided, and an escalated amount is held rather than refunded. Escalation preserves the driver's position for the human reviewer instead of confirming the interim clawback against him on evidence that does not settle the question.

POL-RD-24 provides that exactly one row applies, and its rows divide on the traffic-justification limb: rows (a) to (c) require the reroute to be traffic-justified and rows (d) to (e) require it not to be. With that limb unresolved, no single row can be selected, so this is a case that fits no row, and POL-RD-24 directs that such a case is escalated under POL-GEN-26.

POL-RD-25 allows a route-deviation ruling to stand only at a confidence of 0.80 or more and otherwise sends the case to escalation. With the advisory's intersection unresolved on the artifact that carries it, no monetary ruling on this reroute can be made at that confidence, so the ruling cannot stand and the case must go to a human reviewer with the 1.58 SGD held.

The most the route-deviation matrix can move on this trip is the excess distance fare, and it is 1.58 SGD and no more: POL-RD-24 fixes it as the deviation distance (1.50 km — EV-TRIP-06014's 11.4 km actual minus 9.9 km recommended) multiplied by fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd (1.05 SGD, EV-FARE-06014), without surge. That is precisely the sum already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver, so the driver contests only that 1.58 SGD and claims no part of the 28.94 SGD trip fare.

The driver does not rest his case on the rider having been informed, and the record shows why that limb cannot carry the decision either way without review: no chat notice of the deviation appears in EV-CHAT-06014 — its two messages are both sent before the trip began (18:04:07 and 18:04:37) and both concern the pickup point — and EV-TRIP-06014 records no in-app call, so POL-RD-21's notice requirement is met neither by a chat message nor by a recorded verbal notice. The question this record genuinely leaves open is traffic justification, which is where the case must be sent for review.

The 1.58 SGD clawback was never a final determination: EV-TRIP-06014's fare_adjusted event records the sum as 'refunded to rider and recovered from driver earnings pending review', and EV-FARE-06014 shows the payment status as PARTIALLY_REFUNDED with 1.58 SGD refund_issued_sgd. POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION the confirmation of the present state, and the present state is expressly provisional; the disposition that fits a provisional adjustment is the review POL-RD-25 provides for, not its finalisation against the driver.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the sum in dispute is the 1.58 SGD already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver after the rider's route complaint; the driver filed to contest that clawback, so the outcome is read against him.

Deviation and tolerance (POL-RD-22). Using the platform's recorded distances, the actual route was 11.40 km against a recommended 9.90 km — a deviation of 1.50 km, above the 1.00 km tolerance. The 9.52 km GPS trace is not used to re-measure distance. The trip is therefore not in the no-refund tolerance rows (c) or (e).

The refund matrix (POL-RD-24). The rider was not informed of the deviation. The chat log (EV-CHAT-06014) holds only two messages, 'At City Square Mall taxi stand, silver Lexus' at 18:04:07 and the rider's 'ok' at 18:04:37, both before the trip started at 18:05:37 and both about the pickup; the trip record's in-trip message list and its in-app call list are empty; and the driver's own account is that he did not interrupt the rider. POL-RD-21 requires notice by in-app chat, or a recorded verbal notice, at or before the deviation at 18:14:48, and none is in the record. Row (a) — the only no-refund row for a deviation over 1 km — requires the rider to have been informed and to have agreed, which this record refutes. The two rows that remain for this trip both refund the excess distance fare: row (b) if the reroute was traffic-justified, row (d) if it was not. The money outcome therefore does not depend on whether the CTE heavy-traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-06014-01) is read as intersecting the recommended route, and the case does fit a row either way — so the driver's POL-GEN-26 escalation arguments fail, and the rider's contrary reading (row (d)) reaches the same refund.

The amount (POL-RD-24). 1.50 km x 1.05 SGD/km (EV-FARE-06014), without surge, = 1.58 SGD — exactly the sum already refunded.

Outcome. The rider is owed that 1.58 SGD, so the driver's claim fails and the present state stands: NO_ACTION, with both monetary fields null. The driver's submission that the adjustment was 'pending review' does not change the entitlement, and his claim that POL-RD-21 permits a reroute in response to traffic is answered by the same clause's informing requirement, which was not met, so the deviation was not an agreed one. Confidence is 0.85, above the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires for a route deviation; the contested value of 1.58 SGD is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so no human review is required. No referral clause applies to a route deviation, so the referral list is empty.

ruling.explanation:
Driver D-34123 filed this dispute to recover the 1.58 SGD that Ryde refunded to rider R-43158 and recovered from his earnings after the rider's route complaint. The driver's claim fails and the present state stands: NO_ACTION, with both amounts left null.

What the record shows. The platform's recorded distances (EV-TRIP-06014) give a deviation of 1.50 km — 11.4 km actual minus 9.9 km recommended — which is above the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22, so the tolerance rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 cannot apply. The excess distance fare under POL-RD-24 is 1.50 km x 1.05 SGD/km (the per-km rate in EV-FARE-06014), without surge = 1.58 SGD. That is the whole of the disputed sum; the driver contests no part of the 28.94 SGD trip fare.

Why the reroute was traffic-justified. POL-RD-23 asks whether a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-06014-01) is type HEAVY_TRAFFIC — a congestion type the policy admits — on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards AYE, after the Outram Road exit, valid 17:43:57 to 18:55:37, which overlaps the trip window of 18:05:37 to 18:28:37. The recommended route is Kitchener Road, CTE, AYE, Alexandra Road: the advisory sits on the CTE, in the direction of travel, on the stretch the recommended route uses past the Outram Road exit — the very stretch the driver's diversion avoided. The advisory carries its own road, direction and location and its intersection is a judgment the clause assigns to me, not a gap in the data, so I determine that it intersects the recommended route and the reroute was traffic-justified. The driver's advocate is answered here: his argument that the intersection is 'left open' and that POL-GEN-26 requires escalation is rejected — the advisory is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, the fact is not missing or impaired, and the reason the driver took Outram Road and Henderson Road was congestion on the CTE ahead. The rider's advocate is answered in part: her argument that the case falls in row (d) as not traffic-justified is rejected for the same reason, though the money outcome she seeks is the same.

Why the driver owes the rider's refund. POL-RD-21 requires the driver to tell the rider about a deviation by in-app chat, or verbally with a trip call recording, before or at the point of deviation. The chat log (EV-CHAT-06014) holds only the two pickup messages sent before the trip began, the trip record's in-trip message list is empty, and in_app_calls is empty; the driver's own account — that the rider was on a call the whole ride and he did not interrupt — is an admission that no notice was given. Both advocates agree on this, and I accept it. The case therefore falls in row (b) of POL-RD-24: traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km — refund of the excess distance fare of 1.58 SGD. That is exactly the sum already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver.

Outcome for the party who filed. The 1.58 SGD is owed to the rider and has been paid; the driver's filing asks to have the present state reversed, and on this record his claim is not supported. Under POL-GEN-03 the outcome is read party-relative to the filer, so the ruling is NO_ACTION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both null — the rider keeps the 1.58 SGD. I reject the driver's further argument that the interim 'pending review' label on the fare_adjusted event (EV-TRIP-06014) makes this a case for review rather than a decision: POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION the confirmation of the present state, and the matrix decides the entitlement now.

Confidence, value and referrals. Every artifact I have relied on is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so my confidence is not capped below 1.0 and I set it at 0.85, above the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires for an AI route-deviation ruling. The amount contested is 1.58 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold at which an AI ruling is final at any confidence, and both profiles carry fraud_flags of 0, so no higher bar and no human review follow from value or profiles; the rider's advocate's point on POL-GEN-22 is accepted. No clause in this category produces a referral on these facts, so referrals is empty.

To the driver and to the rider. The driver filed to contest the 1.58 SGD that Ryde refunded to the rider and recovered from him. On this record the rider is owed that sum, so the driver's claim fails and the present state stands: no money moves, and amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd are both null.

Deviation (POL-RD-22). POL-RD-22 fixes the deviation from the platform's recorded distances, 11.4 km actual minus 9.9 km recommended = 1.50 km (EV-TRIP-06014), which is over the 1.0 km tolerance. The sparse GPS trace is not used to re-measure it.

Traffic justification (POL-RD-23). The advisory EV-ADVIS-06014-01 is of type HEAVY_TRAFFIC, a congestion type, valid 17:43:57 to 18:55:37, and it overlaps the trip window. The artifact expressly leaves the intersection question to be decided from the advisory's road, direction and location against the trip: it sits on Central Expressway (CTE) towards AYE, after the Outram Road exit - the very stretch of the recommended CTE route the driver left at 18:14:48 when he took the Outram Road exit (EV-TRIP-06014). It therefore intersects the recommended route and justifies the reroute, so the driver's and the rider's advocates' opposing readings of that limb are resolved in favour of justification. The driver's remark that the route 'saved him time' is not what the clause turns on, and the record in any case shows 23 min against a 20 min recommended time; that neither adds nor removes justification.

Notice (POL-RD-21). The driver gave none. EV-CHAT-06014 holds only two messages, both sent before the trip began (18:04:07 and 18:04:37), and both about the pickup point; EV-TRIP-06014 records no in-app call and an empty messages_during_trip list. The driver's own account, that the rider was on a call so he did not interrupt, is an admission of the same. The rider did not agree to the deviation.

Refund matrix (POL-RD-24). Exactly one row applies: row (b) - traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km - which refunds the excess distance fare, 1.50 km x 1.05 SGD/km = 1.58 SGD (EV-FARE-06014), without surge. That is exactly the sum already refunded and recovered. The rider's advocate read the same advisory as not justifying the reroute, which would put the case in row (d); row (d) refunds the same 1.58 SGD, so the money is the rider's on either reading.

Escalation is not engaged. POL-GEN-26 applies only where a needed fact cannot be established because the evidence carrying it is missing or impaired; here the trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare ledger and traffic advisory are all COMPLETE and carry weight 1.0, and the traffic question is answered from the advisory itself. The deviation. Using the platform's own recorded distances (EV-TRIP-06014), the trip ran 11.40 km against a recommended 9.90 km. That is a deviation of 1.50 km (POL-RD-22), above the 1.0 km tolerance, so the no-refund tolerance rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 cannot apply.

The traffic question. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-06014-01 records heavy traffic on the Central Expressway towards the AYE after the Outram Road exit, valid 17:43-18:55, which covers the trip window (started 18:05:37, ended 18:28:37). The advisory sits on the CTE towards the AYE past the Outram Road exit — precisely the stretch of the recommended route you left, [driver] — so it intersects the recommended route and, under POL-RD-23, the reroute is traffic-justified. The artifact left that intersection for the Judge to decide from its road, direction and location, and on those it falls on the recommended route.

The notice question. POL-RD-21 also requires you, [driver], to tell the rider about the deviation by in-app chat, or verbally with a call recording, before or at the point of deviation. The chat log EV-CHAT-06014 holds only two messages, both sent before the trip began (18:04:07 and 18:04:37) and both about the pickup point; the trip record shows no in-trip message and no in-app call, and you accept you did not interrupt the rider. The rider was therefore not informed, and the deviation is not an agreed one.

What follows. Under POL-RD-24 that is row (b): traffic-justified but the rider not informed, deviation over 1 km — the excess distance fare is refunded. The excess distance fare is 1.50 km x 1.05 SGD/km = 1.58 SGD, with no surge (EV-FARE-06014, POL-RD-24). [Rider], you were right to complain: even if the traffic data were read the other way, row (d) refunds the very same 1.58 SGD, so nothing turns on that question.

Why the driver's claim fails. The 1.58 SGD has already been refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver (EV-FARE-06014, fare_adjusted 2026-10-06T19:16:37). You, [driver], filed this dispute against that refund. Because the rider is owed that 1.58 SGD, your claim is not supported and the present state stands: POL-GEN-03 gives NO_ACTION, with both money figures null — no further refund and no compensation to you. That the adjustment was entered 'pending review' does not change it; NO_ACTION confirms the present state rather than re-opening it.

Why no escalation. The only point left open by the artifact was whether the advisory covers the recommended route; I have decided it does, and in any event both candidate rows pay the same 1.58 SGD, so no fact needed to decide this case is missing or impaired (POL-GEN-26 is not engaged, and POL-RD-24's no-row escalation is not reached). The 1.58 SGD contested is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final on value, and my confidence of 0.90 clears the 0.80 that POL-RD-25 requires. There is no referral: this version attaches none to a route deviation.
